# Hybrid Pi Dispatch: Pane When in a Herdr Session, Headless Fallback Otherwise

## Problem statement

The evaluation of Pi subprocess mechanisms (discovered-from:WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7) found that /skill:audit is dispatched two ways: user-initiated audits open a visible herdr pi pane via send-to-pi.sh, while automated contexts (heartbeat, cron, CI, ssh) must run headless via `pi -p --mode json`. Currently the choice of mechanism is hard-wired per caller and there is no shared way to get a visible pane when a herdr session exists and fall back to a headless subprocess when it does not. The podcast editor (open_source_llm/experimental/herdr-podcast-editor) already implements exactly this hybrid pattern via a HERDR_ENV check; it is a proven precedent to generalise.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want agent work to be visible whenever a herdr session is present, even when the invocation originates from a script or automated context.
- **Skills authors / plugin authors** — want a single reusable dispatch primitive instead of maintaining two mechanisms.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when an audit is triggered from a context that has a herdr session available, I want it to open in a visible pi pane so I can watch it."
- "As a producer, when no herdr session is available, I want the same invocation to fall back to headless execution so the work still happens."
- "As a plugin author, I want to dispatch a skill to pi once and have it choose pane-vs-headless automatically."

## Expected behaviour

- A shared dispatch helper determines at runtime whether a herdr session/pane environment is available (e.g. HERDR_ENV or herdr CLI/socket presence, mirroring the podcast editor).
- When available: dispatch via send-to-pi.sh (visible pane).
- When unavailable: fall back to `pi -p --mode json` headless execution with the same command.
- Existing callers keep their behaviour; new callers (e.g. heartbeat audits, user-initiated audits outside the worklist) opt in.

## Suggested implementation approach

- Add the helper to the shared herdr scripts (packages/herdr/shared/) and/or a small skill-level utility so both herdr code and skills can use it.
- Model the fallback on the podcast editor's send-to-pi.sh wrapper + direct-subprocess branch.
- Wire the heartbeat audit dispatch to use the hybrid helper (pane when herdr present, headless otherwise), which also delivers visibility (see WL-0MSG5THFC004WJEI).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A shared dispatch helper exists that selects pane vs headless at runtime based on herdr availability.
2. With a herdr environment present, dispatch opens a visible pi pane running the given command.
3. Without a herdr environment, dispatch runs the command headless via `pi -p --mode json` and returns programmatic output.
4. At least one existing caller (e.g. heartbeat audit dispatch) is converted to use the helper without regressing its current behaviour.
5. Tests cover both branches (herdr present / absent).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

# Show plugin version in Herdr work item selection list (WL-0MSGKEBFU004T3N3)

## Problem statement

The Herdr Worklog work item selection list gives no indication of which plugin version is running, making it hard to verify installs, spot stale builds, or report bugs accurately. A dimmed, right-aligned version number in the pane header solves this without visual clutter.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who want to confirm which version of the Worklog Selection List plugin is running.
- **Developers/support** who need the version handy when filing bug reports or verifying an updated build is live.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to see the plugin version in the corner of the work item list, so I can confirm which build I'm running.
- As a developer, I want the version visible but unobtrusive, so it doesn't distract from the list content.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The work item selection list header shows the plugin version (`0.1.0` from `packages/herdr/package.json`), right-aligned to the pane width.
2. The version is rendered in the dimmed ANSI style (`\x1b[2m`), matching the existing `[auto-refresh on]` treatment, and does not interfere with the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title.
3. The version is read at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` (not hardcoded in the renderer), so it stays in sync with the manifest version.
4. Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover the header rendering with the version suffix, including a case without a version available (graceful fallback).
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Unobtrusive: dimmed font, right-aligned to the pane edge; must not change existing header content or alignment of the title.
- Use existing patterns: `termSize.cols` for pane width, `ANSI.dim` for dimming, `readFileSync` for reading `package.json` (pattern already used in `worklist.ts`/`shortcut-config.ts`).
- No changes to `herdr-plugin.toml` version unless a version bump is explicitly requested.
- Do not update CHANGELOG.md (managed automatically by the ship skill release pipeline).

## Existing state

- The selection list header is rendered in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (~line 1585): ` Work Items — N item(s)` plus optional `[auto-refresh on]` (dimmed) and `[paused — hidden]` indicators.
- `termSize` (with `cols`) is available in the render function; `truncateLine()` handles width overflow.
- The plugin version is declared in two places: `packages/herdr/package.json` (`"version": "0.1.0"`) and `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` (`version = "0.1.0"`). There is currently no runtime version constant.
- Existing header tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (lines ~86–100) assert `'Work Items'` presence.

## Desired change

1. Add a runtime helper that reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (e.g., parse JSON, fall back to a safe default like `'?'` or omit when unreadable).
2. In the list-mode header renderer, append a dimmed `v<version>` string right-aligned to `cols` (using padding), while keeping the title left-aligned.
3. Add unit tests covering: version suffix present and right-aligned, dim style applied, graceful fallback when the version can't be read.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Header rendering; add version read + right-aligned dimmed suffix (near line 1585).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Header assertions for version suffix, alignment, and fallback.
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — Version source (`0.1.0`); no change expected.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Optional: document the version display.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP** — Create a work item selection list in Herdr: parent feature that produced `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **WL-0MQHYI4E60075SQT** — Fix icon prefix alignment in Pi TUI work item selection list: related header/line formatting work (Pi TUI counterpart).
- **WL-0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ** — Herdr selection list refreshes immediately when its tab regains focus: related Herdr list behavior work.
- **WL-0MQL0T5TR0060AEH** — Add activity-indicator footer to Worklog Pi extension: related footer/status UI precedent (Pi TUI counterpart).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKX5ZV3D0OHIIX2** – Add regression tests for mouse click crash and TUI behavior (completed)
- **WL-0MKZ34IDI0XTA5TB** – TUI: Reparent items without typing IDs (completed)
- **WL-0MQL0T5TR0060AEH** – Add activity-indicator footer to Worklog Pi extension (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/tests/test_ralph_loop.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, src, using, version, work
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2-enforce-git-worktree-usage-for-all-imple/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, using, version, work
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, using, version, work

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: `package.json` is present next to the compiled/tsx module at runtime; the module-dir relative read pattern (as in `shortcut-config.ts`) works for both `npx tsx` and `dist` runs.
- **Risk**: ANSI codes in a right-padded line can misalign padding calculations if padding is computed on raw text length; must compute visible-width padding before applying ANSI styles.
- **Risk**: Very narrow panes could crowd the header; the version suffix should be dropped or truncated if it would overlap the title (guard on `cols`).
- **Scope creep risk**: Bumping the version, adding the version elsewhere (footer/status bar), or showing `wl`/ContextHub versions — out of scope; record as follow-up work items if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1**: "Which version number? I assume the plugin's own version (`0.1.0` from `packages/herdr/package.json` / `herdr-plugin.toml`) — or did you mean the `wl` CLI version or ContextHub's version?"  
  **Answer** (user): "yes the plugins" — the Worklog Selection List plugin's own version. Source: interactive reply.

- **Q2**: "Placement preference? Unobtrusive, dimmed — candidates: (a) right side of the header line, (b) footer hint line, (c) bottom-right corner."  
  **Answer** (user): "a (right aligned to width of pane)" — right-aligned in the header line. Source: interactive reply.

# Herdr metadata panel: drop duplicate ID row from data section

## Problem statement

In the herdr work item selection list, the metadata panel for the selected item shows the work item ID twice: once in the panel title/header line (`── WL-XXXX ──`) and again as the first row of the metadata data table (`ID  WL-XXXX`). The ID row in the data table is redundant and should be dropped, leaving the ID only in the panel title line.

## Users

Users navigating work items in the herdr selection list (`prefix+l`).

**User story:** As a user browsing work items in the herdr selection list, I want the item ID shown once in the metadata panel so the panel is not redundant and the layout is cleaner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The metadata data table in the herdr metadata panel no longer contains an `ID` row.
- [ ] The metadata panel title/header line (`── WL-XXXX ──`) still shows the item ID.
- [ ] Other metadata rows (Status, Stage, Priority, Title, etc.) render unchanged.
- [ ] The detail view (`formatDetailContent`) behavior is unchanged (it already omits ID/Title from its table since they appear in its header).
- [ ] Tests are added/updated covering the metadata panel output (e.g. the `formatMetadataPanel` describe block in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix should follow the existing pattern used by the detail view (`formatDetailContent` filters `ID`/`Title` out of the table since they are in the header).
- No behavior change to the CLI `show` output or other renderers.

## Existing state

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:

- `formatMetadataPanel` (line ~874) renders the panel header separator `── ${item.id} ──` (line ~891) and then the metadata table from `buildMetaRows(item)` (line ~894).
- `buildMetaRows` (line ~828) unconditionally adds the ID as the first row via `addMeta('ID', item.id)` (line ~835).
- The detail view `formatDetailContent` (line ~969) already filters `ID` and `Title` out of the shared table because both appear in its header: `.filter(([label]) => label !== 'ID' && label !== 'Title')`.

So the metadata panel currently shows the ID in both the header line and the first data row — the inconsistency with the detail view.

## Desired change

Remove the `ID` row from the metadata table rendered in the metadata panel, consistent with how `formatDetailContent` handles it. The header line `── WL-XXXX ──` continues to display the ID. The `Title` row should remain in the metadata panel table since the panel header does not show the title.

Likely approach: in `formatMetadataPanel`, filter the `ID` row from `buildMetaRows(item)` output (e.g. `.filter(([label]) => label !== 'ID')`), mirroring `formatDetailContent`. Alternatively, remove `addMeta('ID', item.id)` from `buildMetaRows` — but note `formatDetailContent` relies on `buildMetaRows` including ID then filtering it, so removing it from the shared builder is also safe as long as tests are updated. Prefer the filter-in-panel approach for minimal blast radius.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatMetadataPanel` (~line 874) and/or `buildMetaRows` (~line 828); the ID row is added at line ~835.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — `formatMetadataPanel — field rendering and scrolling` describe block (~line 896); add a test asserting the data table no longer contains an `ID` row while the header still shows the ID. Existing test `expect(joined).toContain('WL-RICH1')` may still pass via the header, but a negative assertion is needed.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X** — "Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command" (completed): introduced the metadata panel and shared `buildMetaRows` (origin of the ID duplication).
- **WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9** — "Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section" (open): also touches metadata section presentation.
- **WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3** — "Show description preview in herder plugin selection list" (open): related to the selection list metadata area.
- **WL-0MNK7CB3F0008YT3** — "Display work item ID in TUI metadata block" (completed): the deprecated Blessed-TUI predecessor; closed as wont-fix/deprecated — not to be used as a pattern.

(Note: an automated find-related scan flagged WL-0MQCU6R6V008JX62, WL-0MRERDU1J000W1IS, WL-0MM0DBM6I1PHQBFI and README worktree copies; these were false positives from keyword overlap and are not genuinely related — excluded per conservative policy.)

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "metadata section" refers to the herdr selection-list metadata panel (the only place showing the ID both in a title line and as the first data-table row). The CLI `show` output shows ID once in its metadata table with no separate ID-bearing title line, so it is out of scope.
- Low risk: change is localized; detail view and CLI outputs are unaffected.
- Scope creep: do not change icon consistency (tracked by WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9) or add description previews (tracked by WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3) in this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which metadata section is this about?" — Answer (user): "The metadata section has the ID in the title line and in the first line of the data section. Drop it from the data section." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: the herdr metadata panel, whose title line is `── <id> ──` and whose first data-table row is `ID  <id>`. Verified against `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (lines 891 and 835).
- Q: "Should the Title row remain in the metadata panel table?" — Assumption (agent, Map): Yes — the panel header shows only the ID, not the title, so Title is not duplicated and stays. Source: code inspection of `formatMetadataPanel` header (line 891 shows only `item.id`). Documented in Desired change.
data.title: Herdr metadata panel: drop duplicate ID row from data section

data.description: When install-herdr.sh appends the [[keys.command]] prefix+l -> worklog-selection-list.open-worklist block to ~/.config/herdr/config.toml, the running herdr server keeps its startup keybindings in memory and does not watch the config file (confirmed in herdr v0.7.5 source: config loaded once at startup via Config::load() in server/headless.rs:4202; only server.reload_config re-reads it). The script prints 'Inserted herdr keybinding ...' with no reload hint, so the binding appears dead until the user manually runs 'herdr server reload-config' or restarts the server. Fix: after writing the config, run 'herdr server reload-config' (best-effort, ignore failure) and/or print a clear hint that a reload/restart is required. AC: re-running the installer makes the prefix+l binding immediately active in a running server without manual reload; script still works when no server is running (skip reload gracefully).

## Summary

Ensure the herdr audit-freshness predicate enforces the canonical "at-or-near"
semantics and is the **single source of truth** shared by both the icon display
and the downtime (audit-dispatch) worker.

Audit freshness currently lives only in `isAuditFresh()` in
`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`. It is the basis for the icon display
(`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) AND is the documented freshness gate reused by the
downtime dispatch audit tier (`selectAuditCandidate` /
`getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, which
treats `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` as "needs a fresh `/skill:audit`").

Running an audit itself bumps the work item's `updatedAt` to within a fraction
of a second of its `auditedAt` (`wl audit-set` + `wl update --audit-text` +
the verdict-driven status transition). A freshness rule that requires a strict
gap on one side (e.g. only `auditedAt` comfortably ahead of `updatedAt`) can
therefore disagree with the just-persisted state. The canonical fix in
SorraAgents (SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4) treats an audit as fresh when its
`auditedAt` is **at or near** the item's `updatedAt` (within a small
tolerance) because a near-simultaneous `updatedAt` bump is the audit's own
persistence write.

This item makes ContextHub's herdr audit-freshness logic follow the same
at-or-near rule so the icon display and the downtime dispatcher agree, and
never disagree on a just-persisted audit.

## Expected behaviour

- `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true (fresh) when `auditedAt`
  is at-or-near `updatedAt` within a small, named tolerance (the audit's own
  persistence write), and false otherwise.
- The icon (`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) shows the fresh icon for a
  just-persisted audit (no longer shows the stale glyph for an audit the run
  just persisted).
- The downtime audit candidate selection (`selectAuditCandidate` /
  `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`) uses the SAME
  `isAuditFresh` predicate, so a just-persisted fresh audit is NOT a dispatch
  candidate (no redundant `/skill:audit` re-run).
- Only one freshness definition exists; neither consumer re-implements its
  own comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `isAuditFresh` in `icons.ts` treats `auditedAt` at-or-near `updatedAt`
   (within a documented tolerance constant) as fresh, covering the
   audit-persistence case (`auditedAt ~ updatedAt`, delta well under the
   tolerance).
2. A unit test asserts `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` is true for a
   just-persisted audit (auditedAt and updatedAt differ by milliseconds).
3. A unit test asserts a genuinely stale audit (item updated well after the
   audit) is still false (stale), unchanged.
4. `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`
   continue to use the imported `isAuditFresh` as the sole filter; a
   just-persisted fresh item is excluded from candidates.
5. Both consumers import the same helper; no competing freshness comparison
   is introduced in the dispatch or icon paths.

## Notes / Open questions

- `isAuditFresh` currently hard-codes a magic `60000` ms literal. Prefer
  naming a constant (e.g. `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`) and routing
  both consumers through it.
- Reconcile the comparison shape of `isAuditFresh` (`auditTime > updateTime -
  buffer`) with the canonical at-or-near semantics from the SorraAgents fix so
  both projects express the same intent. Confirm the target semantics with the
  operator before implementing.

## References

- discovered-from: SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 (SorraAgents audit_runner child
  freshness at-or-near fix) — canonical reference implementation.
- related-to: WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31 (Audit candidate selection),
  WL-0MSI9WPNI0044R (Audit dispatch tier), parent WL-0MSI8H3HP700K0RG.
data.title: Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher

## Problem statement

SorraAgents is the canonical installer for pi agent guidance: its scripts/install_pi.sh symlinks the global guidance (AGENTS_GLOBAL.md -> ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md, plus skills and prompts) into every project. The global AGENTS.md already contains the full agent workflow (work-item lifecycle, implement/build-test-commit order, push policy, triage policy).

ContextHub's 'wl init' (src/commands/init.ts) currently has overlapping responsibilities: it prompts for a workflow choice (promptWorkflowChoice: N / B / M, where M is 'Manage custom workflow by editing AGENTS.md directly') and, via ensureWorkflowTemplateInstalled / insertWorkflowLoaderIntoAgents, can inline WORKFLOW content into the project's AGENTS.md. When the SorraAgents global install is present this creates two sources of truth for agent workflow guidance and can conflict with the canonical global file.

## User story

As a developer running wl init on a machine with the SorraAgents install, I want wl init to delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup to the SorraAgents install so the global guidance is the single source of truth and the project AGENTS.md only carries project-specific content.

## Desired change

- When the SorraAgents global install is detected (i.e. ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md resolves to a SorraAgents AGENTS_GLOBAL.md symlink), wl init should NOT inline workflow content into the project AGENTS.md. Instead it should emit/keep the canonical reference structure used by SorraAgents projects:
  - '## Global agent guidance' section referencing ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md
  - '## Project-specific guidance' section for local rules
- wl init should either invoke the SorraAgents install (scripts/install_pi.sh) or clearly document that the SorraAgents install is the canonical mechanism, rather than duplicating guidance.
- The existing pointer-line behavior from 'wl init: prefer global AGENTS.md pointer' (WL-0MLD6N0GW12MNKK0) must be preserved and aligned with the canonical structure above.
- Standalone Worklog users without the SorraAgents install keep the current workflow options (N/B/M) unchanged.

## Success criteria

1. With the SorraAgents global install present, running wl init in a fresh project does not inline WORKFLOW content into AGENTS.md; the file carries the canonical global-reference structure only.
2. wl init output/help documents the SorraAgents install as the canonical global-guidance mechanism (delegation), with no duplicated workflow content.
3. Without the SorraAgents install, existing wl init workflow behavior (N/B/M) is unchanged and existing tests pass.
4. Tests cover both environments (with and without the global SorraAgents symlink).
5. Full ContextHub test suite passes.

## Related work

- ContextHub: 'wl init: prefer global AGENTS.md pointer' (WL-0MLD6N0GW12MNKK0, completed) established the pointer-line behavior this item extends.
- SorraAgents: 'AGENTS.md installer: emit single reference line for new projects' is the complementary installer-side item; the AGENTS.md split (AGENTS_GLOBAL.md canonical source + symlink install) landed in SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W.

# Intake Brief: Colour code work items by priority in selection lists (CLI + Herdr)

**Work Item ID:** WL-0MSJ2JFMO007PGQ6

**Headline:** Colour coding of work items in the selection list should be based on **priority**, not stage: critical are red, low are dimmed, medium is white, high is orange — recorded in a shared theme file.

## Problem Statement

Work item titles in selection lists are currently coloured by **stage** (progression: gray → blue → cyan → yellow → green → white, from WL-0MQ53H78W000DQ08). Stage progression communicates workflow position, but operators scanning a list need to see **priority** at a glance — critical items should jump out in red, low-priority items should recede. The colour scheme must be defined once in a shared theme file.

## Users

All Worklog users viewing work item lists:

- **Operators and agents** scanning `wl list` / `wl search` / `wl recent` need immediate visual cue of what matters (critical = red, high = orange).
- **Herdr users** browsing the Worklog selection list pane need the same priority cue.

Example user stories:
- "As an operator, I want critical work items to appear red so I can immediately spot what needs attention."
- "As an agent, I want low-priority items dimmed so they recede while scanning the list."
- "As a project manager, I want a consistent priority colour scheme across the CLI and the Herdr selection list, defined in one shared theme file."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The canonical priority colour mapping is recorded in the shared theme file `src/theme.ts`:
   - `critical` → red
   - `high` → orange
   - `medium` → white
   - `low` → dimmed
2. Work item **titles** are coloured by priority and work item **ids** are coloured by stage, everywhere they appear: `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl recent`, `wl show`, `wl next`, and the Herdr worklist selection list (`formatItemLine`).
3. Blocked items no longer receive the unconditional red override; they are coloured by their natural priority like every other item (per clarification Q3b).
4. Unknown/missing priority falls back to a sensible default colour (e.g. medium/white) and unknown/missing stage keeps a sensible default (gray) — matching current fallback behaviour.
5. Unit tests cover the new priority colour mapping and the title/priority + id/stage split in both the CLI helpers (`src/commands/helpers.ts`) and the Herdr icons (`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`), including blocked and unknown-priority cases.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- The Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr/`) is a separate package depending only on `@worklog/shared`; it renders raw ANSI 256-colour escape codes and cannot import `src/theme.ts` (which depends on chalk).
- The Pi-based TUI extension (`packages/tui/`) is **out of scope** — it is slated for removal (see WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N) and colours via Pi theme tokens, not the theme file.
- "Orange" should use a colour consistent with the existing `theme.text.readyNo` (`chalk.hex('#FFA500')`).
- No new dependencies.

## Existing state

- `src/theme.ts` already has a `priority` map (`critical: chalk.redBright`, `high: chalk.yellowBright`, `medium: chalk.blueBright`, `low: chalk.gray`), a `stage` progression map, and a `blocked: chalk.redBright` override.
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — `renderTitle()` colours the title by stage (`titleColorForStage`), with a blocked override checked first; `formatTitleAndId()` renders the id muted (`theme.text.muted`); `humanFormatWorkItem()` also renders ids muted in several formats.

## Summary

`wl sync`'s merge logic can enter a self-sustaining conflict loop that silently corrupts item state. Observed in the field (LP-0MSDRRPV0001TCLX in /home/rgardler/projects/llm): a completed, audit-approved item's local `updatedAt` advanced at every sync (21:36:19Z → 21:53:40Z → 21:57:35Z) and the final sync chose a local `deleted` state (empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) over the remote `open` state — soft-deleting the item while the remote `worklog/data` ref still had it `open`/`plan_complete`. No agent ran `wl delete`; the state arose purely from merge behavior. The item had to be manually restored via `StatusLifecycle`.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verified against src/sync.ts)

1. **Same-timestamp merge bumps `updatedAt` unconditionally.** `mergeSameTimestampItems` (src/sync.ts ~L423) sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content (e.g. a `sortIndex` conflict from concurrent `wl re-sort`, or any divergent field). This bump makes the item *newer* than the remote on the next sync, so the local value keeps winning and the timestamp keeps advancing on every sync — a conflict loop with no real user edit behind it. Under auto-sync / multi-pane / multi-agent use this can repeat indefinitely.

2. **Unattributed soft-delete wins over a live remote item.** `deleteSingle` (node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts) sets `status: 'deleted'` but leaves `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` empty. In `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `status` is resolved by plain timestamp recency: `status='deleted'` is a non-default value, so if the local copy is (artifactually) newer, `status` flips to `deleted` even though `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` are empty — silently soft-deleting an item the remote still considers open. There is no delete-side equivalent of the close-preservation logic that protects `status='completed'`/`stage='done'`.

## Expected behaviour

- Repeated syncs of the same divergent state must converge: once both sides hold the merged item, `updatedAt` must stop advancing and the item must not flip-flop.
- An unattributed delete marker (status='deleted' with empty deletedBy/deleteReason) must never override a remote item that is open/in-progress/completed. Deletes should only propagate when they are real, attributed deletes (non-empty deletedBy or deleteReason), mirroring the close-preservation model.

## Suggested approach

- In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field (or converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side). Consider whether `sortIndex` conflicts alone should bump at all.
- Add delete-side protection in `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (and same-timestamp path): treat `status='deleted'` like `status='completed'` — require the delete to be the newer change AND attributed (deletedBy/deleteReason non-empty) before propagating it; otherwise keep the remote live status.
- Add regression tests in tests/sync.test.ts reproducing both failure modes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing only in `sortIndex` or one metadata field) synced repeatedly converge — `updatedAt` stops advancing after the merged state is present on both sides (no unbounded bumping).
- AC2: Regression test: local `status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` vs remote `status='open'` — merge keeps the remote `open` state (or at minimum never produces a soft-deleted item with no attribution).
- AC3: Regression test: an *attributed* delete (non-empty `deletedBy`) that is newer than the remote still propagates (delete remains possible when intentional).
- AC4: Full existing test suite (npm test) passes with no regressions.

# Prevent top line info bar from scrolling off screen (WL-0MSNI6TQ5003JY1Z)

## Headline

Fix the Herdr plugin's top `Work Items` info bar wrapping off screen in narrow panes by truncating the header to the terminal width so it never exceeds one row.

## Problem statement

In the Herdr `worklog-selection-list` plugin's list mode, the top info bar (row 0: `Work Items — N item(s) [auto-refresh on] [Downtime Off]` plus optional `(filtered: …)`, `(top …)`, `[paused — hidden]` and code-freeze banners) can exceed the pane width in narrow terminals. The header is assembled by string concatenation without truncation, so when its visible length exceeds `cols` the terminal wraps it onto extra physical rows. When total rendered output then exceeds the `rows - 1` line-count invariant (WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO), the terminal scrolls the first line off the top of the pane and the header is not visible — even with the minimal `[Downtime Off]` status and no idle timestamp.

## Users

- **Herdr worklist users** browsing the selection list in narrow panes (e.g. 80 cols or less, `herdr pane layout` narrow split), who rely on the top bar to see the item count, active filter, auto-refresh and downtime state.

### Example User Stories

- As a Herdr user with a narrow pane and many items, I want the top `Work Items` info bar to stay visible at row 0 regardless of pane width or list content, so I don't lose the item count and system status.
- As a Herdr user, I want a long header (filter + auto-refresh + downtime) to be truncated with an ellipsis rather than wrapping onto a second row and pushing the header off screen.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Header never wraps / always visible at row 0:** In list mode, the header line is truncated to fit the terminal width (visible length ≤ `cols`, ANSI preserved via `truncateLine`) so it occupies exactly one output row. For any `cols` ≥ 40 and any combination of `filterLabel`, `totalCount` (`top N of M`), `autoRefresh`, `panePaused`, and `downtimeStatus` (`[Downtime Off]`, `[Downtime Off (restored)]`, `[downtime paused]`, `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]`, `[downtime busy]`, `[⏳ downtime dispatching]`), `renderer(…)` output satisfies `stripAnsi(output.split('
')[0]).includes('Work Items')` and `stripAnsi(output.split('
')[0]).length <= cols`.

2. **Line-count invariant holds in narrow panes:** In list mode the full renderer output contains at most `rows - 1` newline-separated lines for any `TermSize` (e.g. 40×24, 80×24, 120×53, 60×20) and any list state (short list, full list, scrolled list, with/without banners, with/without fold indicators `▲/▼ more`, with minimal and maximal header length). No render exceeds the pane height and the top line is never scrolled off.

3. **No regression in other modes:** Detail-mode rendering (`formatDetailView` and renderer detail path with pinned header+ToC) and filter-mode rendering are unchanged — existing tests for the pinned ToC (WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S / WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I), `'keeps the ToC pinned at the top while the document scrolls'`, and filter prompt still pass with no behavior change.

4. **Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`:** Cover (a) header truncation at narrow width — visible length ≤ `cols` and `Work Items` text still present for a long header at 40 cols and 60 cols; (b) line-count invariant (`lines.length <= rows - 1`) for list mode at narrow width (40×24) with a long header, with banner active, and without banner; (c) wide-pane sanity (80×24 / 120×24) still passes — no over-truncation for short headers.

5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant README/docs entries describing the header layout (`packages/herdr/README.md`).**

6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Surgical fix in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `createListRenderer` list-mode header path only — do not change detail/filter rendering or the dynamic list/metadata panel layout beyond the header fix.
- Reuse the existing `truncateLine(line, maxWidth)` helper (ANSI-aware) — no new dependencies or truncation implementations.
- Preserve ANSI styling (bold Work Items, dim/colour for status segments) when truncating; the ellipsis `…` must close open ANSI codes via `ANSI.reset` as `truncateLine` already does.
- Must preserve the `rows - 1` invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO — the fix must not add chrome rows; the header must remain a single chrome row.
- No change to `renderDowntimeStatus` idle timer growth — truncation must remain correct as the `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]` string grows (regression guard).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `createListRenderer` (around lines 3217–3229) builds the list-mode header:
  ```ts
  let header = ` ${ANSI.bold}Work Items${ANSI.reset} — ${totalItems} item(s)${filterLabel}`;
  if (totalCount !== undefined && totalCount > totalItems) { header += ` (top ${totalItems} of ${totalCount})`; }
  if (autoRefresh) { header += ` ${ANSI.dim}[auto-refresh on]${ANSI.reset}`; }
  if (panePaused) { header += ` ${ANSI.fg(220)}[paused — hidden]${ANSI.reset}`; }
  if (downtimeStatus) { header += downtimeStatus; }
  output.push(header);
  ```
  The header is pushed without `truncateLine(…, cols)`, unlike banners (`truncateLine(bannerLine, cols)`) and footer/tooltip lines. When `visibleLength(header) > cols`, the pty wraps it onto a second physical row so `output` logically has `rows - 1` lines but physically occupies `rows` or more, scrolling the first line off the top (observed in narrow panes even with minimal `[Downtime Off]` content, and exacerbated by `codeFreezeActive` banners, long `filterLabel` like `(filtered: stage in_review)`, or large `totalCount`).

- Detail view header/ToC is already pinned (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I / WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S): `formatDetailView` pins `DETAIL_HEADER_LINES + tocLines` at the top and only the body scrolls — not affected by this list-mode header issue.

- Prior fix WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO corrected layout accounting for group separators and notification-line overflow, and WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ accounted for `▲/▼ more` indicators in the `budgetForRows` budget — but neither guarded the header's own width.

- `truncateLine` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:1224`) is ANSI-aware and already used for banners; `renderDowntimeStatus` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:3077`) returns ANSI-wrapped status strings of varying length.

- No existing tests assert the header's visible length constraint at narrow widths; the overflow only appears visually in the pty and is not caught by current line-count tests which use wide (80/253) cols.

## Desired change

1. In `createListRenderer` list-mode branch (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` ~3220–3233), apply the existing `truncateLine` to the assembled header before pushing it:
   ```ts
   header = truncateLine(header, cols);
   output.push(header);
   ```
   (Keep the existing `output.push` as a single row; do not add a second header row.)

2. Verify the fix maintains the `rows - 1` invariant when the header is long — the header now costs exactly one line regardless of `cols`, so no additional chrome accounting is needed, but the safety clamp at the end of the renderer (`while (output.length > rows - 1) output.pop()`) remains as a backstop.

3. Do not change `renderDowntimeStatus`, `computeDynamicLayout`, `formatDetailView`, or the detail/filter render paths.

4. Update code comments on the header assembly to note the truncation guard and narrow-pane wrap prevention (reference this work item and WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO).

5. Add narrow-pane unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` per AC 4 and ensure all existing tests remain green.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `createListRenderer` list-mode header assembly (`Work Items …` concatenation and `output.push(header)`) and `truncateLine` helper; primary fix location.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Add header truncation and narrow-pane `rows - 1` invariant tests (list mode, with/without banners, varying header lengths); keep existing detail pinned-ToC tests green.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Update if it describes the header/status bar layout; otherwise code-comments only.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO** — "Herdr plugin: selection list header and top lines cut off top of pane" (completed, critical) — introduced the `rows - 1` / `rows` line-count invariant and corrected separator/notification accounting; this item extends the same invariant to the header's own width.
- **WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S** — "Detail view ToC overflows pane — first lines scroll off the top of the screen" (completed) — the detail-view analogue with pinned header+ToC; this list-mode header fix is the list-mode counterpart and must not regress that fix.
- **WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I** — "Detail view ToC for Related Docs" (completed) — introduced the pinned ToC design preserved by the previous item.
- **WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ** — "Herdr selection list: no indication of items below the fold" (completed) — introduced `▲/▼ more` indicators with explicit `budgetForRows - indicatorRows` accounting; relevant to the chrome budget near the header.
- **WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J** — "Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls" (completed) — introduced `computeDynamicLayout` and the `chromeLines = 2 + bannerCount` budget that the header consumes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: Over-truncation hides useful status.** Mitigation: `truncateLine` preserves the leading `Work Items — N item(s)` prefix and only drops trailing status segments; at 40 cols the most informative prefix remains visible and full status is available in wider panes. Document the truncation behavior.
- **Risk: `truncateLine` double-counts ANSI vs display width.** Mitigation: reuse the proven `truncateLine` implementation already used for banners; add a test that asserts visible length (via `stripAnsi`) after truncation, not raw string length.
- **Risk: Growing idle timer (`m:ss`) eventually pushes other segments off.** Mitigation: tested as part of the variable-length `downtimeStatus` combinations; the truncation guard is independent of which status variant is active.
- **Risk: Breaking existing line-count tests that assume header length.** Mitigation: widen the test cols or update expectations to account for truncation — no functional change for 80+ cols where the header already fits.
- **Assumption:** The reported wrap is in **list mode** (the main `Work Items` list), not in detail mode — confirmed by operator (Q4/Q5). If detail-mode header wrapping is later reported, a separate item should cover it.
- **Assumption:** Narrow pane is the primary reproduction (`cols ~ 40–80`); the fix is validated at 40 cols as the lower bound (below 40 the pane is pathological and the existing `while (output.length > rows - 1) output.pop()` backstop applies).
- **Scope creep:** A richer fix could elide individual status segments (e.g. hide `[auto-refresh on]` first, then downtime) instead of raw truncation — explicitly out of scope for this bug; file as a follow-up enhancement if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When you say 'the info line at the top,' are you referring to the metadata table (Status, Priority, Stage, etc.) that sits below the pinned header in the detail view?" — Answer (user): "I mean the very first line, it contains the Work Items count, the auto-refresh status, the downtime status." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 1, Q1. Research: inspected `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `createListRenderer` header assembly (lines 3217–3229); top line is `Work Items — N item(s) [auto-refresh on] [Downtime …]` plus optional filter/paused segments.
- Q: "Should the fix pin the metadata table as well (so only the description/document viewer scrolls), or is there a different line/section you have in mind?" — Answer (user): "No." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 1, Q2.
- Q: "How many items should be in scope — just the metadata table in the detail view, or also the list-mode metadata panel at the bottom of the pane?" — Answer (user): "It has nothing to do with the meta-data (see 1)." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 1, Q3. Research: confirmed the issue is the list-mode header, not any metadata panel/table; detail view already has a pinned header+ToC via WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S.
- Q: "When this happens, is it the main list header (`Work Items — N item(s)...`) or a different line? And does it happen during normal list mode, or specifically when you're in the detail view for an item?" — Answer (user): "4 main" (i.e. the main list header). Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 2, Q4. Research: `createListRenderer` list-mode branch pushes `header` as `output[0]`; detail-mode path returns via `formatDetailView` and never renders the `Work Items` header.
- Q: "Does it happen with narrow terminal windows (e.g., 80 cols), or also at wider widths?" — Answer (user): "5. Narrow." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 2, Q5. Research: wide pans (253 cols) have ample space for the header; narrow panes (40–80 cols) reproduce the wrap — banners and long filter labels exacerbate it.
- Q: "Does the downtime status text include a timestamp that grows as time passes (e.g., `[downtime idle m:ss]`) — could this growing timestamp eventually cause the header line to wrap?" — Answer (user): "6. no - happens event when it says `[Downtime Off]`." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 2, Q6. Research: `renderDowntimeStatus` (worklist.ts:3077) returns `. [Downtime Off]` (shortest variant) when the worker is disabled — wrap reproduces even with this minimal segment, confirming the bug is not timer-growth-specific; discovered a typo in the answer ("event" = "even") and did not alter the captured intent.

## Summary

## Root cause

`packages/herdr/tsconfig.json` sets `rootDir: ./src` and includes `src/**/*.ts`, which includes the `.test.ts` files. - [ ] `cd packages/herdr && npm run build` exits 0.
- [ ] `dist/shortcuts.json` is copied on every build.

# Intake Brief: Herdr hydrator — rescue in_progress work items with no active pane

## Headline

Add a hydration task to the herdr worklist plugin that, every 30 seconds, fetches all `in_progress` work items, matches each against the work-item IDs embedded in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace (via the pane-title work WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y), and demotes any item with no matching pane out of `in_progress` to `completed` (stage `in_review`), `blocked` (dependency-blocked), or `open` (otherwise). The check also runs immediately when the tab regains focus.

## Problem statement

Work items are sometimes left stuck in `status=in_progress` even though no agent pane is actually working on them (e.g. the agent pane was closed, the session died, or the item was claimed and abandoned). There is currently no automatic mechanism to detect this, so stale in-progress items linger at the top of work queues and are never re-selected.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want a self-healing work queue where an item only stays `in_progress` while an active agent pane is genuinely attached to it.
  - As a producer, I want items whose agent pane has died to be demoted automatically so they re-enter the selection pool instead of rotting in `in_progress`.
- **Herdr worklist users** — benefit from a queue that reflects reality without manual cleanup.
  - As a user, I want the worklist to keep `in_progress` items only when a matching pane exists, so the list stays honest.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every 30 seconds the hydrator fetches all `in_progress` work items (`wl list --status in_progress`).
2. For each item, the hydrator attempts to match an **active pane**: a pane, in **any tab of the current workspace**, whose pane title contains the work item's ID (`WL-…`) and that is still running (present in `herdr pane list`). Matching relies on the pane-title format introduced by the blocking work item (e.g. `Manually triggered implement <title> - WL-<id>`).
3. Any `in_progress` item with **no matching active pane** is demoted:
   - stage `in_review` → `status=completed`
   - item has an active outbound dependency blocker (target not `completed`/`deleted`, not stage `in_review`/`done`) → `status=blocked`
   - otherwise → `status=open`
   Transitions respect the project's status/stage compatibility rules (e.g. `blocked` only allows stages `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`, so a stage `in_progress` item demoted to `blocked` must also have its stage demoted).
4. When the worklist tab regains focus, the hydration check runs **immediately** (not waiting for the next 30s tick), reusing the existing visibility resume-poll mechanism.
5. The hydrator is **safe**: no transition is made for an item whose matching pane is found; the task is single-flight; failures (CLI missing, unparseable output) are logged and never crash the plugin; no `wl` spawns happen while the worklist pane is hidden.

# Intake Brief — Replace binary author-identity gate with configurable author whitelist (WL-0MTGDW58X007UJDS)

## Problem Statement

`wl sync` currently uses a binary author-identity gate (`syncAllowForeignAuthor` boolean): it either allows only commits from the local `user.email` or allows all foreign authors. This causes false-positive refusals for single operators with multiple emails/machines and does not scale for team or CI scenarios that need a selective allow-list.

## Users

- **Single operator, multiple machines/emails** — wants sync to succeed when their own secondary email appears on the remote without opening the gate to everyone.
- **Team lead / shared repo** — wants to allow a known set of collaborators' emails while still rejecting unknown authors.
- **CI / automation** — wants to allow a bot email in addition to the human operator without disabling the gate entirely.

### Example User Stories

- As a developer with `sorra@thewizardscode.com` on laptop and `alice@company.com` on CI, I want to whitelist both emails in `.worklog/worklog.yaml` so `wl sync` merges remote commits from either without requiring `--allow-foreign-author` on every run.
- As a project maintainer, I want the default (`syncAllowedAuthors: []`) to preserve the strictest behavior (only local `user.email`) so existing single-author repos see no security regression.
- As an operator who previously used `syncAllowForeignAuthor: true` or `--allow-foreign-author`, I want that flag to keep working (mapped to allow-all) so I am not broken by the migration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Config schema:** `syncAllowedAuthors` is accepted in `.worklog/config.yaml` / `config.defaults.yaml` with validation: `[]` (empty list, default), non-empty string list, `null`, or `true` (allow-all). Invalid types are rejected with a clear error.
- [ ] **AC2 — Gate behavior:** Empty list enforces current behavior (only local `user.email` accepted); non-empty list accepts any email in the whitelist; `null`/`true` allows any author (equivalent to current `--allow-foreign-author`). Empty-author commits are always refused regardless of whitelist.
- [ ] **AC3 — CLI compatibility:** `wl sync --allow-foreign-author` still works and overrides the config to allow-all for that invocation; help text (`wl sync --help`) explains the whitelist model (`[]` default, list, `null`/`true` allow-all) and the flag's override semantics. Existing `--allow-foreign-author` users are unaffected.
- [ ] **AC4 — Tests:** Automated tests cover: empty-list strict gating, non-empty whitelist allows listed / rejects unlisted, `null`/`true` allows all, empty-email always refused, and CLI flag override. Existing sync author-gate tests continue to pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Docs & suite:** Help text and relevant docs (e.g. `SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` / `CONFIG.md` or equivalent) describe the whitelist model. All related documentation and code comments are updated. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Default `[]` must preserve current security posture — no widening of the gate for existing repos without explicit config change.
- Empty author email is never bypassed (neither whitelist nor `--allow-foreign-author` nor `null`/`true` allows it).
- Backward compatibility: `syncAllowForeignAuthor` boolean and `--allow-foreign-author` flag must keep working; migration should not break existing users. Prefer whitelist as canonical, boolean as deprecated alias or mapped value.
- Email comparison should be case-insensitive (or documented as case-sensitive if intentionally strict) — assumption: case-insensitive, trimmed comparison.
- Minimal scope: config + gate logic + CLI flag wiring + help/docs + tests. No changes to merge logic beyond the gate.

## Existing State

- Author-identity gate lives in `src/sync.ts` (`checkAuthorIdentity`, `enforceAuthorIdentityGate`, `getConfiguredUserEmail`, `getRemoteAuthorCommits`) and is wired in `src/commands/sync.ts` via `getSyncDefaults` / `performSync` → `enforceAuthorIdentityGate`.
- Config key `syncAllowForeignAuthor?: boolean` is defined in `packages/shared/src/types.ts` and consumed in `src/commands/sync.ts` (`getSyncDefaults`). No `syncAllowedAuthors` exists yet.
- `src/config.ts` loads/merges `config.defaults.yaml` + `config.yaml` and validates statuses/stages; no whitelist validation.
- Related work: WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB (identity gate), WL-0MSUEO62N0019P3S (checkAuthorIdentity), WL-0MSUEOAQO0081TJH (wire gate + flag + sync-point), WL-0MTGH78A4000ZVNB (refusal verbosity/exit).

## Desired Change

- Add `syncAllowedAuthors?: string[] | null | true` to `WorklogConfig` (canonical whitelist). Keep `syncAllowForeignAuthor` as deprecated alias that maps to `null` (allow-all) when `syncAllowedAuthors` is unset, or document precedence.
- Add `syncAllowedAuthors: []` (or commented example) to `config.defaults.yaml` (test fixture defaults) and update validation in `src/config.ts` to accept `[]`, `string[]`, `null`, `true`.
- Replace binary gate in `src/sync.ts` (`checkAuthorIdentity` / `enforceAuthorIdentityGate`) to read the whitelist from config: `[]` → only `user.email`; non-empty → `user.email` plus listed emails; `null`/`true` → allow all (except empty-email).
- Update `src/commands/sync.ts` `getSyncDefaults` and CLI registration so `--allow-foreign-author` overrides to allow-all (and optionally `--sync-allowed-authors` or equivalent if desired; at minimum flag → allow-all). Update help text to explain whitelist model.
- Update docs (`SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` and/or `CONFIG.md` / `DATA_SYNCING.md`) and add tests covering AC4.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — Add `syncAllowedAuthors?: string[] | null | boolean` to `WorklogConfig`; keep `syncAllowForeignAuthor` as deprecated alias
- `src/config.ts` — Validate/normalize `syncAllowedAuthors` (allow `[]`, `string[]`, `null`, `true`); merge with defaults
- `src/sync.ts` — Modify `AuthorIdentityOptions` / `checkAuthorIdentity` / `enforceAuthorIdentityGate` to enforce whitelist instead of pure boolean
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — Wire `syncAllowedAuthors` via `getSyncDefaults`; keep `--allow-foreign-author` as allow-all override; update help text
- `src/sync-defaults.ts` / `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml` (test fixture) — Add default `syncAllowedAuthors: []` and/or documentation
- `docs/sync/SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` (or `CONFIG.md` / `DATA_SYNCING.md`) — Document whitelist model
- `tests/sync-author-gate.test.ts` / `tests/cli/sync-author-gate.test.ts` — Add whitelist coverage

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB** — Sync: identity gate — refuse merge of foreign/empty-author commits (completed) — parent feature this refines
- **WL-0MSUEO62N0019P3S** — Implement checkAuthorIdentity gate in src/sync.ts (completed)
- **WL-0MSUEOAQO0081TJH** — Wire identity gate into wl sync + config flag + sync-point persistence (completed)
- **WL-0MTGH78A4000ZVNB** — Author-identity gate refusal must surface at default verbosity and exit non-zero (completed)
- **WL-0MTGH7ALW002BOQN** — Recovery path for already-diverged worklog repos (completed)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk — Ambiguous precedence:** Both `syncAllowForeignAuthor` and `syncAllowedAuthors` could be set. Mitigation: define clear precedence (whitelist wins when set; boolean is deprecated alias / maps to `null` only when whitelist absent); document and test.
- **Risk — Email normalization:** Case/whitespace differences could cause false refusals. Mitigation: trim + case-insensitive comparison; document.
- **Risk — Scope creep:** Temptation to add regex/wildcard matching or per-branch whitelists. Mitigation: out of scope; record as follow-up work items if requested.
- **Assumption — `null` and `true` are equivalent allow-all** per proposed solution; `undefined`/absent means default `[]`.
- **Assumption — Empty-email gate remains unconditional** (never bypassed).
- **Assumption — No new CLI flag for the list needed in v1**; whitelist is config-only, CLI flag remains allow-all override. A `--sync-allowed-authors` flag can be a follow-up.

## Appendix — Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should `syncAllowForeignAuthor: true` be deprecated or kept indefinitely?" — Answer: Keep for backward compatibility; treat as alias that maps to `syncAllowedAuthors: null` when whitelist is unset. Precedence: explicit `syncAllowedAuthors` wins. Source: Proposed solution AC + existing-state analysis; no producer input yet — recorded as assumption.
- Q: "Should email comparison be case-insensitive?" — Answer: Assumed case-insensitive trimmed comparison (common for emails). Alternative (case-sensitive) would cause surprising refusals; document choice. Source: assumption, to be confirmed if producer prefers strict matching.
- Q: "Is a CLI flag to set the whitelist needed (e.g. `--sync-allowed-authors a@x,b@y`)?" — Answer: Not required for v1; whitelist is config-only, `--allow-foreign-author` covers the allow-all escape hatch. CLI list flag can be a follow-up if requested. Source: scope constraint, inferred from proposed solution.

- `src/sync.ts`
- `src/commands/sync.ts`
- `src/config.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts`
- `src/sync-defaults.ts`
- `docs/sync/SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md`
- `tests/sync-author-gate.test.ts`

# Downtime dispatcher: make wl-error pauses debuggable

## Problem
Between 01:00–now 2026-09-02 the TCE per-worklog `downtime-dispatches.log` showed 5 aggregate pauses:

`"Downtime worker: 3 consecutive wl CLI errors — pausing dispatch for 3600000ms."`

with successful dispatches interleaved (01:47 audit, 02:14 implement, 02:44 intake, 03:14 audit, 03:47 implement, 04:14 plan, 05:44 implement) — proving transient failures. **No per-strike detail is retained**, so "what was the wl error?" cannot be answered from logs.

Root cause: `DowntimeErrorEvent` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1093` `{cwd,at,message}`) has no error field; `pauseAfterPersistentErrors(message)` (`downtime-worker.ts:2547` -> `fetcher.ts:372`) is called with the fixed string `wl CLI errors — pausing dispatch…` (`downtime-worker.ts:2921`), discarding the `Error(message)` built from `stderr||stdout||error.message` at `fetcher.ts:372` and the per-entry `result.ok===false` skip at `downtime-worker.ts:1634` / `wl-error` outcome at `1559`. Only the 3-strike aggregate is written via `deps.recordError()` -> `appendDowntimeLogEntry()` (`index.ts:998`/`downtime-log.ts:268`), with no stderr/exitCode/timeoutMs/workItemId/probe context.

Machine-wide dispatch is now authoritative (`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` + `downtime-leader-lease.json`), but logs stay per-worklog (`downtime-log.ts:5` F6 WL-0MTII4CWT00452HU + `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md:222`) for per-project observability — aggregate + per-strike logs must be queryable.

## Desired change
- Extend `DowntimeErrorEvent` (and/or add a per-strike structured event) to capture: last `stderr`/ excerpt, `exitCode`/worklogRoot`, `command` (e.g. `wl show <id>`), `attempt` (1/3), and probe context (`coordination empty` vs direct `dispatchDowntimeWork`).
- Log **each** wl-error strike (not only the 3rd) to the rolling JSONL so the 5 pauses become 15 diagnosable lines, while retaining the existing pause marker for alerting (bounded to `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES=100`).
- Distinguish coordination probe failures (`computeMostImportantItem` -> `downtime-worker.ts:2896` ``worklog probe failed…``) from dispatch-path `wl-error` so operators can tell `empty file transient gap` vs `CLI failure`.

- [ ] A 3-strike pause produces the existing pause line plus 3 per-strike lines, each with parseable stderr/exitCode/timeout and workItemId, visible via `grep wl-error */.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.

# Scheduled prompts: add time-of-day dispatch (time window) to scheduled-prompts tier

## Problem statement

The scheduled-prompts tier (WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX; `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, `templates/scheduled-prompts.json`) only supports best-effort frequency in whole days (`intervalDays` via `isDueScheduledPrompt`: due iff `now - lastTriggeredAt >= intervalDays`). There is no way to pin a prompt to a time of day, so a daily standup cannot be made to run at a specific wall-clock time (e.g. 06:05) and instead fires whenever the next idle slot appears after the interval elapses — too early/late for a daily standup window.

## Users

- Operators who want a prompt (notably the daily standup, `/skill:standup`) to run at a specific time of day, not just once per N days whenever an idle slot appears.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want to add an optional `time` field (e.g. `06:05`) to a scheduled-prompt entry so the system dispatches it in the first available idle window **after** that time, so the standup runs at 06:05 each day.
- As an operator, when `time` is absent the existing behaviour is unchanged (due iff `now - last >= intervalDays`), so existing entries like `/skill:refactor` keep working without config changes.
- As an operator, I want `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` and provisioned `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` to set `/skill:standup` to 06:05, so a fresh worklog gets the correct daily standup time.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add optional `time?: string` to `ScheduledPrompt` (`packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts`). When absent, behaviour is identical to today (backward-compatible). Valid values are wall-clock `HH:MM` 24-hour times (e.g. `06:05`); entries with an invalid `time` are skipped with a logged warning (fail-closed, never a crash), consistent with invalid `intervalDays`/prompt handling (AC7 of WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX).
2. Extend due-check semantics (`isDueScheduledPrompt` / `getDueScheduledPrompt`): an entry with `time` is due only when BOTH (a) `now - lastTriggeredAt >= intervalDays * DAY_MS` (same interval gate as today) AND (b) `now` is at or after the `time` on the calendar day of `now` (local wall-clock). If `now` is before `time` today and the interval gate is otherwise satisfied, the entry is NOT due — it becomes due in the first idle window at/after `time`. A dispatched entry is NOT due again until the next calendar day's `time` has been reached and the interval has again elapsed (so a 06:05 daily entry dispatched at 07:00 today is not due again at 08:00 today).
3. `lastTriggeredAt` semantics ensure once-per-interval: after a timed dispatch, the interval comparison uses the actual dispatch time, so a missed `time` (e.g. no idle slot until 08:00) still counts as dispatched for that day and the next due time is tomorrow 06:05 (not 08:00 tomorrow and not immediately). Daily entries with `time` therefore fire at most once per calendar day.
4. Update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` to include `/skill:standup` with `intervalDays: 1` and `time: "06:05"` (the canonical standup time). `src/commands/init.ts` provisioning remains create-if-absent; `wl init` on an existing repo must not clobber user edits — if the operator has customised scheduled prompts, re-running `wl init` leaves them untouched. New worklogs provisioned after this change get the timed standup entry.
5. Ensure `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` in the current checkout reflects `time: "06:05"` for `/skill:standup` (so the dev branch's live config matches the template).
6. Update documentation/comments to describe the `time` field (README / `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` header / `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md` or equivalent downtime docs) and the "first window after time" semantics, including the backward-compat note when `time` is absent and the local wall-clock interpretation of `HH:MM`.
7. Unit/integration tests cover: parse of `time` (valid, absent, invalid → skipped), due-check with `time` (before-time not due, at/after-time due, interval gate interaction, once-per-day, missed-window becomes tomorrow), backward-compat (no `time` behaves as before), and the timed standup entry in the provisioned template.
8. Full project test suite passes with the new changes (no regressions).

## Constraints

- Follow the worker's existing fail-closed philosophy at every boundary: never dispatch, never throw (mirrors WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX constraints and `scheduled-prompts.ts` header).
- `time` is wall-clock local `HH:MM` (no timezone field, no cron); `lastTriggeredAt` remains UTC ISO-8601 as today. The due check interprets `time` against local calendar day.
- Scheduled tier remains the first dispatch tier, gated by the same fresh-read code-freeze marker; per-process single-flight guard still applies. No new timer infrastructure — reuse `createDowntimeWorker.tick`.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — `ScheduledPrompt` (id/prompt/intervalDays/lastTriggeredAt), `parseScheduledPrompt`, `isDueScheduledPrompt`, `getDueScheduledPrompt`, `DAY_MS`; no `time` field.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` scheduled tier (freeze gate → scheduled → audit → …); `dispatchScheduledPrompt` with atomic `lastTriggeredAt` persist + rolling-log `scheduled` kind.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` + `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — base set is `/skill:refactor` (intervalDays 3) plus `/skill:standup` (intervalDays 1) with no `time`.
- `src/commands/init.ts` — provisions `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` from the template, create-if-absent (never clobber).

## Desired change

Extend `ScheduledPrompt` with optional `time: "HH:MM"` and update the due-check to be "interval gate AND at-or-after time today" so timed entries dispatch in the first idle window after their wall-clock time. Set the canonical standup time to `06:05` in both the template and the live `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`. Update docs/tests accordingly. When `time` is absent, behaviour is identical to today.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — add `time` field, validation, due-check extension.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — no structural change expected (consumes via `getDueScheduledPrompt`), but verify tier interaction / dispatch semantics for timed entries.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` — add `time: "06:05"` to `/skill:standup`.
- `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — add `time: "06:05"` to `/skill:standup` in the checkout so the dev branch reflects the template.
- `src/commands/init.ts` — no change expected beyond carrying the new template value (create-if-absent preserved).
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.test.ts` or `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — new/updated tests for `time` parse + due-check.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` / `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md` / `CONFIG.md` / `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` header — document `time` field and "first window after time" semantics.

## Related work

- WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX — scheduled prompts tier (parent capability).
- Standup skill: `/skill:standup` + `generate_standup.py` (scheduled via this tier; canonical consumer of `06:05`).
- WL-0MTF5UAJ4000LLZ9 — provisioning / scheduled-prompts template.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: `time` is `HH:MM` local wall-clock on the calendar day of `now`; seconds are not needed. `lastTriggeredAt` remains UTC — the due check bridges them by comparing the local clock for `time` against `now` and the interval against `lastTriggeredAt`.
- Risk: "first window after time" depends on an idle slot appearing; if the machine is busy all day, the dispatch slips to the next idle window (still at most once per day due to `lastTriggeredAt` anchoring). This is the correct best-effort behaviour.
- Risk: DST / system clock skew — acceptable for best-effort `HH:MM` local semantics; clock-skew handling mirrors `isDueScheduledPrompt` today (future `lastTriggeredAt` → not due).
- Scope creep: cron expressions, timezone-aware schedules, per-entry model overrides — record separately, not this item.

## Problem statement

`runCoordinationCheckIn` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` re-offers only every `DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS = 30min` (`downtime-worker.ts:235,2645,2843` — `lastCheckInAt` gate, startup + `>=30min`). That's the only place `computeMostImportantItem()` → `upsertEntry()` offers a new item (1 per project per 30min, not configurable via `settings.ts`). `dispatchFromCoordination` removes the dispatched entry immediately, leaving a transient empty gap until the owner re-offers.

The dispatcher itself can dispatch every `~70s` while idle (`DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=10s` jittered ±50% + `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS=60s`, `worklist.ts:downtime` task not `paneGate.visible()`-gated, `createDowntimeWorker.tick()` idle gate). So even after WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P removes the `300s` `pruneStaleEntries` expiry (`dispatchFromCoordination:1638`, `DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS`), offers remain the bottleneck: with 4 projects, a burst of ~4 dispatches in ~4min when idle, then ~26min gap until next check-ins. Within one project, back-to-back items cannot dispatch continuously at the idle rate.

This follow-up to WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P shortens the offer cadence so the leader always has work to dispatch while idle, without reintroducing age-based expiry.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — expects spare-capacity dispatch to keep the machine busy while idle, not idle 26min of every 30min because offers are sparse.
- **Herdr user with multiple project tabs** — wants fair `critical first then round-robin` at the configured idle rate, not bursts gated by 30min check-ins.
- **Maintainer** — needs a single consistent contract: offers persist (WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P) and are refreshed fast enough to keep up with dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Check-in interval shortened** — `DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS` reduced from `30min` to `5min` (or otherwise `<=5min`; integration test already uses `300_000` at `integration-leader-dispatch.test.ts:316`). Lower bound `>=60s` to avoid wl churn. `checkInIntervalMs` remains injectable via `DowntimeWorkerConfig` for tests.
2. **Post-dispatch re-offer** — when `dispatchFromCoordination` removes an entry (`removeEntry` on dispatched or claimed-but-failed spawn/marker), the owning instance re-offers its next `computeMostImportantItem` without waiting for the next interval (push-based). Minimal hook: leader notifies owner via coordination file observation, or owner watches its own entry removal on next `tick()` and immediately runs `runCoordinationCheckIn` (no extra poll when not idle). Fail-safe: file read failure still degrades to next interval.
3. **No expiry reintroduced** — `pruneStaleEntries` removal from WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P stays; this item does not reintroduce TTL pruning. Eligibility still validated at dispatch time (`fetchItem`+`classifyItemForDispatch`/`isAuditFresh` per WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P).
4. **Rate still gated by idle/slots** — dispatch still requires `evaluateIdle` + `perSlotTracker.thresholdMetCount` + `freeSlots >= DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS / DOWNTIME_PANE_MIN_FREE_SLOTS`; faster offers do not bypass idle or slot budgets. Probe semantics `WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7` (coordination empty = transient gap) unchanged.
5. **Tests & build green** — `downtime-worker`/`coordination-dispatch`/`integration-leader-dispatch` fixtures updated for new default interval and re-offer hook; `npm run build` + herdr suite green. Manual spot: overnight log shows >1 dispatch per 10min while idle with multiple projects offering.
6. **Docs updated** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` downtime section document new interval and re-offer behavior.

## Constraints

- Depends on WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P (expiry removal); do not reintroduce `pruneStaleEntries` for coordination entries.
- Do not touch ranking — `WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2` owns `dispatcher == Herdr list head`; reuse `computeMostImportantItem` pipeline.
- Fail-safe: unreadable coordination/lease files still degrade to no dispatch this cycle, never crash. No new npm deps.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:235` `DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS = 30*60*1000`, `:2645` `checkInIntervalMs = opts.checkInIntervalMs ?? DEFAULT...`, `:2843` `lastCheckInAt` gate, `:1830` `runCoordinationCheckIn` (fail-open on `!ok`, removes entry on `noCandidate`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `downtime` scheduler task (poll `~10s` jittered, idle `60s`, not visibility-gated) → `createDowntimeWorker.tick()` → `dispatchFromCoordination` (tier `audit→critical(sortIndex)→implement→plan→intake`, `sortEntriesByRoundRobin` per `worklogRoot`).
- `WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P` removes `pruneStaleEntries(..., leaseTtlMs=300s)` (`:1638`, `DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS`) and adds dispatch-time `fetchItem` eligibility gate — leaves 30min offer sparsity.
- Tests: `integration-leader-dispatch.test.ts:316` uses `300_000` to stay inside old prune window; `coordination-dispatch.test.ts:667,784,834` assumes `30min` cadence.

## Desired change

1. Lower `DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS` to `5min` (clamped `>=60s`).
2. Add immediate re-offer after dispatch: after `dispatchFromCoordination` removes the dispatched entry, the owner (on its next `tick()` or via a file-watch of its own `instanceId`) runs `runCoordinationCheckIn` out-of-band so the next idle window has a fresh offer. Implement as `tick()` check: if `getEntry(coordDir, instanceId) == null` and not in `noCandidate` cooldown, run `runCoordinationCheckIn` immediately (fail-open).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS`, `createDowntimeWorker` `lastCheckInAt` gate, `dispatchFromCoordination` remove path, `runCoordinationCheckIn`
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — `getEntry`/`upsertEntry`/`readCoordinationFile` used by re-offer check
- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` — unchanged (leadership lease only)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `downtime` scheduler interval unchanged (offer refresh is worker-internal)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` — contract docs
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/integration-leader-dispatch.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`

## Related work

- WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P — remove coordination entry expiry; validate eligibility at dispatch time (critical, depends on)
- WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V — fair round-robin, WL-0MTJE0FXC006WAOX — per-root cursor
- WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7 — empty-file vs empty-backlog probe
- WL-0MTF0KLO10043YAN — machine-wide leader, WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 — dispatcher == Herdr list head

## Goal

Add a single machine-wide dispatch/coordination audit log maintained by the downtime leader, so dispatch history can be queried in one place (`last 2 hours?`) instead of stitching per-project logs.

## Problem Statement

Currently the authoritative state lives in the machine dir `~/.herdr/downtime/` (`downtime-coordination.json`, `downtime-leader.lock`, `downtime-leader-lease.json`, `downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`) while dispatch/coordination logs stay PER-ROOT at `<cwd>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` and `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` (retained by F6 decision WL-0MTII4CWT00452HU for per-project observability; the worklog comment on the item is the durable cross-machine trail). Debugging a machine-wide leader required `grep` across 5+ per-root logs to answer "what was dispatched in the last 2 hours" — ContextHub was quiet while open_source_llm dispatched 10 items in the same window. The leader (single machine-wide election) is the natural single writer for a central log.

## User Stories

- As an operator, I want `last 2h of dispatches across ALL projects` from one file so I don't have to grep 5 per-project `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` files.
- As a maintainer, I want the leader's decisions (skip reasons, strikes, cooldowns) in one place to correlate pause behaviour across projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A bounded rolling JSONL log exists at `<machine-dir>/downtime-dispatches.log` (default `~/.herdr/downtime/`) and is appended by the leader path (`dispatchFromCoordination`) for every dispatch attempt and outcome (itemId, kind, worklogRoot, dispatchedAt, stage, outcome/reason, error detail).
2. A non-leader (legacy mode, no coordinationDir) still writes its per-root `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` unchanged (backward compatible; the per-root file remains the dispatched-marker source for `auditDispatchedItemIds` / `implementDispatchedItemIds` — those readers are NOT migrated).
3. Coordination operations (checkin/election/prune/offer) are also appended centrally OR a `--machine` reader merges the per-root coordination logs; the central file is authoritative for "what happened machine-wide".
4. Expose `wl downtime log --machine --since <duration>` (or equivalent CLI) that prints central + per-root entries newest-first with cwd, without requiring a grep across files.
5. The central log is fail-closed: append failure never crashes the worker (mirrors `appendRollingJsonl` fail-safe contract); bounded to most recent `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES`.
6. The audit-tier dispatched-marker readers (`readDowntimeLogEntries`/`auditDispatchedItemIds`) keep reading the PER-ROOT log so per-project exclusion behaviour is unchanged (AC2).
7. Unit tests: leader appends a central entry per dispatch across multiple worklog roots; bounded rolling; fail-closed on unwritable machine dir; legacy non-leader path untouched; a `--since 2h` query across roots returns merged entries.

## Constraints

- The machine coordination dir is the single source of truth for leadership (do not create a second election).
- Do not remove or relocate the per-root logs (marker readers depend on them); the central log is an ADDITION for observability.
- Follow `appendRollingJsonl` bounded-append pattern and fail-closed contract.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — add machine-dir log writer/reader (reuse `appendRollingJsonl` with the machine dir).
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — machine dir resolver (already exists).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchFromCoordination` + worker tick: append central entry on dispatch/outcome/skip/strike.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wire CLI command + settings.

## Existing State

- `~/.herdr/downtime/` currently holds only: `downtime-coordination.json`, `downtime-leader.lock`, `downtime-leader-lease.json`, `downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` (no central log today).
- Per-root `downtime-dispatches.log` (100-line bounded) written by `appendDowntimeLogEntry`; `downtime-coordination.log` by `appendCoordinationLogEntry`.
- Decision F6 WL-0MTII4CWT00452HU: coordination file/lease migrated machine-wide, logs deliberately NOT migrated — this item is a deliberate follow-up to add a central log for machine-wide debugging while keeping per-root logs.

## Related Work

- WL-0MTII4CWT00452HU (F6 migration), WL-0MTF0KLO10043YAN (single machine-wide leader), WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 (dispatch audit log), WL-0MSXHAE290067VAL (coordination log), WL-0MTOCBP1D009P4U3 (leader check-in), WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 (Herdr list-head dispatch).

## Risks & Assumptions

- Assumption: keeping per-root logs AND adding a central one is acceptable duplication; marker readers never read the central file.
- Risk: central log writes contend on the machine dir — mitigated by the existing lock + bounded append (fail-closed).
